cover.lead: No sorted array? Binary search the answers when every answer past one point works.

blog.summary: When every value past some point works, binary search the possible answers for the first one that does.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (the LeetCode 875 examples, one pile, piles at 10⁹ with tight and loose hours, all piles equal, hours equal to the number of piles), 10,000 random piles up to 10⁹, 10,000 piles of 10⁹ (where the total hours pass the 32-bit limit), and random small cases
blog.tested_against: a brute force that tries every speed from 1 up (and, for huge piles, a library binary search over the same check)
blog.tested_extra: The speeds in the walk-through, the hour counts, the quick-check answer and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: Binary search on answers explained: find the slowest speed that still finishes in time (LeetCode 875 Koko Eating Bananas).
lines: There's no sorted array, but the answers are in order: slow speeds fail, and once one works, every faster one works.
The trap: round the hours down and piles 3 6 7 11 in 8 hours give speed {{wrong_min_speed(PILES, HOURS)}} instead of {{ANSWER}}.
caption.cta: Which problem have you seen that hides an answer to search?
